outputs.L2: A radiological imaging system comprises a gantry that forms an examination region for receiving a body portion of a patient and defines a circular path about a central axis. The gantry houses a radiation source that generates radiation, a detector that captures the radiation after it traverses the examination region, and an enclosure providing an internal space for the source and detector. The enclosure is formed by a lower curved module and a curved movable module that can shift relative to the lower module, thereby changing the enclosure’s angular span. A module-actuation mechanism is also provided. This mechanism includes a lower guide fixed to the lower curved module and establishing a lower circular travel path centered on the central axis, a movable guide fixed to the movable curved module and establishing another circular travel path centered on that axis, and a drive assembly that interacts with the guides to control rotation of the curved modules about the central axis.
outputs.L3:
The radiological imaging device comprises a gantry defining an analysis area configured to accommodate at least a portion of a patient. The gantry extends along a substantially circular trajectory around a central axis and supports a radiation source and a corresponding radiation detector arranged to acquire radiological images of the patient.

The radiation source and detector are housed within a casing comprising a bottom arched module and a movable arched module. The movable arched module is displaceable relative to the bottom arched module, thereby allowing the angular extension of the casing around the central axis to be adjusted. This configuration enables the casing to be selectively opened or closed to facilitate patient access while maintaining the geometry required for imaging.

A movement apparatus controls the relative displacement of the arched modules. The apparatus includes a circular bottom guide associated with the bottom arched module, a circular mobile guide associated with the movable arched module, and a thrust assembly configured to act between the guides. Operation of the thrust assembly causes the movable arched module to rotate around the central axis relative to the bottom arched module, enabling controlled adjustment of the casing’s angular extension.
outputs.L4:
The radiological imaging device comprises a gantry configured to accommodate at least part of a patient within an imaging region. The gantry supports a radiation source and a corresponding radiation detector positioned so that radiation emitted by the source passes through the patient before reaching the detector. Depending on the imaging procedure, the source and detector may be arranged on opposite sides of the imaging region and moved around the patient to acquire projection data from different angular positions.

The gantry includes an adjustable casing that encloses or protects at least part of the imaging components while allowing the shape and extent of the gantry to be modified. The casing is formed by a fixed arched module and at least one mobile arched module. These modules extend along respective circular arcs and are associated with concentric circular guides. The concentric arrangement enables the mobile arched module to rotate relative to the fixed arched module while maintaining a substantially uniform path around the imaging region.

A thrust assembly is coupled to the mobile arched module and selectively drives its rotation along the circular guides. The thrust assembly may move the mobile module in either angular direction and hold it at a desired position. As the mobile module rotates, it can overlap the fixed module to a greater or lesser degree. This movement changes the overall angular extension of the casing around the patient without requiring the entire gantry to be displaced.

In a more closed configuration, the arched modules collectively surround a larger angular portion of the imaging region, thereby providing increased coverage and protection for the internal components. In a more open configuration, the mobile module is retracted relative to the fixed module, reducing the casing’s angular extension and creating a wider access area. Intermediate configurations may also be selected according to the examination, the patient’s anatomy, or the need for medical personnel to reach the patient.

The adjustable casing therefore provides a gantry architecture that combines imaging capability with improved physical access. It can facilitate patient positioning, simplify entry into and removal from the imaging region, and permit access during interventional or image-guided procedures. By controlling the mobile arched module through the thrust assembly, the device can adapt the gantry opening while preserving the alignment and concentric movement of the casing components.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. It is known as the definite article and is used to refer to a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” points to a particular book that the speaker and listener can identify.

Although it contains only three letters, “the” plays an important role in communication. It adds clarity, creates emphasis, and helps connect ideas. Writers also use it in titles and memorable phrases, such as “the future,” “the truth,” or “the one.”

Small and easily overlooked, “the” demonstrates how even the simplest words can have a powerful effect on meaning.

counterfactuals.output: A radiological imaging device comprises a gantry defining an examination region and including a fixed bottom arched module and at least one movable arched module. The movable arched module is coupled to the fixed bottom arched module by circular guides and is displaceable along an arcuate trajectory to vary an angular extension of the gantry. A thrust assembly acts between the fixed bottom arched module and the movable arched module to drive and control movement of the movable arched module between a retracted configuration, facilitating access to the examination region, and an extended configuration, providing increased circumferential coverage. counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an X-ray imaging apparatus in formal technical language, including the patient analysis area, radiation source, detector, adjustable casing, concentric movement guides, and mechanism for rotating the casing modules about a central axis.
counterfactuals.output:
An X-ray imaging apparatus comprises a patient analysis area configured to receive at least a portion of a patient and defining a central examination axis. A radiation source is arranged on a first side of the patient analysis area and is configured to emit an X-ray beam through the patient analysis area. A radiation detector is positioned on an opposing side and aligned with the radiation source to receive radiation transmitted through the patient.

The radiation source and detector are supported by an adjustable casing comprising one or more casing modules. The casing modules are movably coupled to respective arcuate movement guides arranged concentrically about the central examination axis. A drive mechanism, including one or more motors operatively connected to the casing modules through gears, belts, rollers, or equivalent transmission elements, displaces the modules along the concentric guides. Such displacement rotates the casing modules, and the source and detector carried thereby, about the central axis while maintaining their relative alignment. A control system regulates the angular position, rotational velocity, and relative spacing of the modules to permit acquisition of projection images from selected orientations around the patient analysis area.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the structural components and movement system of a radiological scanner with an adjustable annular gantry, using the terminology and style of a European patent application.
counterfactuals.output:
A radiological scanner (1), in particular an X-ray computed-tomography, fluoroscopic or nuclear-imaging apparatus, may comprise the following structural and kinematic assemblies.

The scanner (1) comprises a support structure (2), for example a floor-mounted base or a mobile chassis, and an annular gantry (3) defining a substantially central examination opening (4) through which a patient support (5) is receivable. The annular gantry (3) comprises a stationary annular frame (6) and, preferably, a rotary carrier (7) supported relative to the stationary frame (6) by bearing means (8).

An imaging arrangement is mounted on the rotary carrier (7). In an X-ray embodiment, said arrangement comprises an X-ray source (9) and a radiation detector (10) disposed substantially opposite one another with respect to an imaging axis (A). Rotation of the carrier (7) about the imaging axis (A) enables projection data to be acquired at a plurality of angular positions. In other embodiments, detector modules may be distributed around at least part of the circumference of the annular gantry (3).

The gantry (3) is adjustable relative to the support structure (2) by means of a positioning system (11). The positioning system (11) may comprise:

- at least one guide arrangement (12), such as linear rails, arcuate guides or mutually spaced linkage arms;
- one or more driven carriages (13) coupled to the gantry (3);
- at least one actuator (14), preferably an electric spindle drive, toothed-belt drive, rack-and-pinion drive, hydraulic cylinder or servo motor;
- a transmission arrangement (15) for transferring actuator movement to the gantry; and
- a locking or braking device (16) for retaining the gantry in a selected position.

The positioning system (11) is configured to provide one or more degrees of freedom. These may include vertical displacement along a first axis (Z), transverse displacement along a second axis (X), longitudinal displacement along a third axis (Y), and/or pivotal movement about a substantially horizontal tilt axis (B). The tilt axis (B) may extend through, or adjacent to, the annular gantry (3), thereby permitting the imaging plane to be inclined relative to the patient support (5). The gantry may additionally be pivotable between an operative position and a parking or patient-access position.

The rotary carrier (7) is driven independently of the gantry-adjustment movement by a rotary drive (17), for example a direct-drive motor or a motor coupled to the carrier by a belt or gear transmission. Electrical power and data signals may be transferred between the stationary frame (6) and the rotary carrier (7) by a slip-ring assembly (18), rotary transformer or contactless data link.

Position sensors (19), such as encoders, linear transducers or angular sensors, detect the position of the gantry (3) and the rotary carrier (7). A control unit (20) controls the actuators (14, 17) in response to operator commands and stored examination parameters. The control unit (20) may coordinate gantry translation, gantry inclination, patient-support movement and rotation of the imaging arrangement. Limit switches, collision sensors and mechanical end stops may be provided to prevent movement outside a permissible range.

Flexible conduits or an energy-chain arrangement (21) guide electrical cables, cooling lines and communication conductors during adjustment of the annular gantry. Counterbalancing means (22), for example springs, gas struts or counterweights, may support at least part of the gantry mass and reduce the load applied to the actuator (14).

Accordingly, the annular gantry is both internally rotatable for acquisition of radiological data and externally positionable relative to the patient and/or support structure. The separation of the rotary imaging movement from the gantry-positioning movement permits the imaging axis and imaging plane to be adapted to the anatomical region under examination while maintaining controlled support and alignment of the source and detector.
